item.title: Downloading and Analyzing GEDI L4A Above-Ground Biomass Data
item.description:
Overview

GEDI L4A (Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation, Level 4A) provides footprint-level estimates of above-ground biomass density (AGBD) in Mg/ha, derived from GEDI’s full-waveform LiDAR measurements. Each footprint is ~25 m in diameter, with ~60 m along-track spacing and ~600 m cross-track spacing.

This tutorial compares GEDI L4A AGBD across two contrasting landscapes:

Region Site Land Cover
Region 1 NEON SCBI — Front Royal, Virginia Temperate deciduous forest
Region 2 Central Park & surroundings — New York City Urban green space

Steps covered:

  1. Define two study areas
  2. Find and download GEDI L4A granules
  3. Read and extract AGBD from HDF5
  4. Quality filtering
  5. Spatial visualization for each region
  6. Side-by-side comparison

Setup

# Install required packages (run once)
install.packages(c("rGEDI", "hdf5r", "sf", "terra",
                   "ggplot2", "dplyr", "leaflet", "viridis", "patchwork"))
library(hdf5r)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)   # side-by-side ggplots

Step 1 — Define Two Study Areas

# ── Region 1: NEON SCBI — Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute, VA ──
scbi <- list(
  name    = "NEON SCBI — Front Royal, VA",
  lon_min = -78.20,
  lat_min =  38.85,
  lon_max = -78.10,
  lat_max =  38.95
)

# ── Region 2: Central Park & surrounding urban area — New York City ──
nyc <- list(
  name    = "Central Park & surroundings — New York City",
  lon_min = -74.05,
  lat_min =  40.70,
  lon_max = -73.85,
  lat_max =  40.85
)

regions <- list(scbi = scbi, nyc = nyc)

# Helper: convert region list to sf polygon
region_to_sf <- function(r) {
  st_bbox(c(xmin = r$lon_min, ymin = r$lat_min,
            xmax = r$lon_max, ymax = r$lat_max),
          crs = 4326) |> st_as_sfc() |> st_as_sf()
}

scbi_sf <- region_to_sf(scbi)
nyc_sf  <- region_to_sf(nyc)

Visualize both regions on an interactive map:

leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") |>
  addPolygons(data = scbi_sf, color = "#2d6a4f", weight = 2,
              fillOpacity = 0.15, label = scbi$name) |>
  addPolygons(data = nyc_sf,  color = "#e63946", weight = 2,
              fillOpacity = 0.15, label = nyc$name) |>
  addScaleBar() |>
  fitBounds(-78.20, 38.85, -73.85, 40.85)

Step 2 — Find GEDI L4A Granules

library(httr)
library(jsonlite)

gedi_finder <- function(r) {
  url <- paste0(
    "https://lpdaacsvc.cr.usgs.gov/services/gedifinder",
    "?product=GEDI04_A",
    "&version=002",
    "&bbox=", r$lon_min, ",", r$lat_min, ",", r$lon_max, ",", r$lat_max
  )
  resp     <- GET(url)
  granules <- fromJSON(content(resp, "text"))$data
  return(granules)
}

scbi_granules <- gedi_finder(scbi)
nyc_granules  <- gedi_finder(nyc)

cat("SCBI granules:", length(scbi_granules), "\n")
cat("NYC  granules:", length(nyc_granules),  "\n")

Step 3 — Download Granules

Requires a free NASA EarthData account at urs.earthdata.nasa.gov.

library(rGEDI)

# Download SCBI granules
gediDownload(filepath = scbi_granules, outdir = "data/gedi_scbi")

# Download NYC granules
gediDownload(filepath = nyc_granules,  outdir = "data/gedi_nyc")

Tip: Each granule is ~500 MB–2 GB. For a small bounding box, usually 1–3 granules are sufficient.

Step 4 — Read and Extract AGBD from HDF5

A single reusable function handles both regions:

extract_gedi_l4a <- function(h5_path, region) {

  h5    <- H5File$new(h5_path, mode = "r")
  beams <- c("BEAM0000", "BEAM0001", "BEAM0010", "BEAM0011",
             "BEAM0101", "BEAM0110", "BEAM1000", "BEAM1011")

  results <- lapply(beams, function(beam) {
    if (!beam %in% names(h5)) return(NULL)
    tryCatch({
      b <- h5[[beam]]
      data.frame(
        lon        = b[["lon_lowestmode"]][],
        lat        = b[["lat_lowestmode"]][],
        agbd       = b[["agbd"]][],
        agbd_lower = b[["agbd_pi_lower"]][],
        agbd_upper = b[["agbd_pi_upper"]][],
        quality    = b[["l4_quality_flag"]][],
        degrade    = b[["degrade_flag"]][],
        beam       = beam
      )
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
  })

  h5$close_all()

  bind_rows(results) |>
    filter(lon >= region$lon_min, lon <= region$lon_max,
           lat >= region$lat_min, lat <= region$lat_max)
}

# Extract for SCBI
scbi_raw <- list.files("data/gedi_scbi", pattern = "\\.h5$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  lapply(extract_gedi_l4a, region = scbi) |> bind_rows()

# Extract for NYC
nyc_raw  <- list.files("data/gedi_nyc",  pattern = "\\.h5$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  lapply(extract_gedi_l4a, region = nyc)  |> bind_rows()

cat("SCBI raw footprints:", nrow(scbi_raw), "\n")
cat("NYC  raw footprints:", nrow(nyc_raw),  "\n")

Step 5 — Quality Filtering

quality_filter <- function(df) {
  df |> filter(quality == 1, degrade == 0, agbd >= 0, agbd < 1000)
}

scbi_clean <- quality_filter(scbi_raw)
nyc_clean  <- quality_filter(nyc_raw)

cat("SCBI after filtering:", nrow(scbi_clean), "shots\n")
cat("NYC  after filtering:", nrow(nyc_clean),  "shots\n")

Step 6 — Spatial Maps

NEON SCBI

pal_forest <- colorNumeric("YlGn", domain = c(0, 400), na.color = "transparent")

leaflet(st_as_sf(scbi_clean, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    radius      = 3,
    color       = ~pal_forest(agbd),
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    stroke      = FALSE,
    popup       = ~paste0("<b>AGBD:</b> ", round(agbd, 1), " Mg/ha<br>",
                          "<b>90% PI:</b> [", round(agbd_lower, 1), ", ",
                                              round(agbd_upper, 1), "]")
  ) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal_forest, values = ~agbd,
            title = "AGBD (Mg/ha)", position = "bottomright") |>
  addControl("<b>NEON SCBI — Temperate Forest</b>", position = "topright")

Central Park & NYC Urban Area

pal_urban <- colorNumeric("YlGn", domain = c(0, 200), na.color = "transparent")

leaflet(st_as_sf(nyc_clean, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    radius      = 3,
    color       = ~pal_urban(agbd),
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    stroke      = FALSE,
    popup       = ~paste0("<b>AGBD:</b> ", round(agbd, 1), " Mg/ha<br>",
                          "<b>90% PI:</b> [", round(agbd_lower, 1), ", ",
                                              round(agbd_upper, 1), "]")
  ) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal_urban, values = ~agbd,
            title = "AGBD (Mg/ha)", position = "bottomright") |>
  addControl("<b>Central Park & surroundings — NYC Urban</b>", position = "topright")

Step 7 — Side-by-Side Comparison

AGBD Distribution

# Combine with region label
combined <- bind_rows(
  mutate(scbi_clean, region = "NEON SCBI\n(Temperate Forest)"),
  mutate(nyc_clean,  region = "Central Park / NYC\n(Urban)")
)

ggplot(combined, aes(x = agbd, fill = region)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 15, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2d6a4f", "#e63946"), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "GEDI L4A AGBD Distribution — Forest vs Urban",
    x     = "Above-Ground Biomass Density (Mg/ha)",
    y     = "Number of Footprints"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

Summary Statistics

combined |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    n_shots    = n(),
    mean_agbd  = round(mean(agbd),   1),
    median_agbd = round(median(agbd), 1),
    sd_agbd    = round(sd(agbd),     1),
    min_agbd   = round(min(agbd),    1),
    max_agbd   = round(max(agbd),    1)
  ) |>
  print()

Spatial Scatter (both regions)

p_scbi <- ggplot(scbi_clean, aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = agbd)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "YlGn", name = "AGBD\n(Mg/ha)",
                        limits = c(0, 400), oob = scales::squish) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "NEON SCBI", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

p_nyc <- ggplot(nyc_clean, aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = agbd)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "YlGn", name = "AGBD\n(Mg/ha)",
                        limits = c(0, 200), oob = scales::squish) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Central Park / NYC", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

p_scbi + p_nyc +
  plot_annotation(title = "GEDI L4A Above-Ground Biomass Density",
                  subtitle = "Temperate forest (left) vs urban green space (right)")

Step 8 — Rasterize to 500 m Grid

rasterize_agbd <- function(df, region, res = 0.0045) {
  r_template <- rast(
    xmin = region$lon_min, xmax = region$lon_max,
    ymin = region$lat_min, ymax = region$lat_max,
    resolution = res, crs = "EPSG:4326"
  )
  vect(df, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326") |>
    rasterize(r_template, field = "agbd", fun = "mean")
}

r_scbi <- rasterize_agbd(scbi_clean, scbi)
r_nyc  <- rasterize_agbd(nyc_clean,  nyc)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(r_scbi, col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
     main = "SCBI — Mean AGBD (Mg/ha)", range = c(0, 400))
plot(r_nyc,  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
     main = "NYC  — Mean AGBD (Mg/ha)", range = c(0, 200))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

Key Notes

  • Coordinate system: All GEDI L4A coordinates are WGS84 (EPSG:4326).
  • AGBD fill value: Shots with agbd = -9999 are no-data — always filter before analysis.
  • Prediction interval: agbd_pi_lower / agbd_pi_upper give the 90% prediction interval per footprint.
  • Power vs coverage beams: Power beams (BEAM0101, BEAM0110, BEAM1000, BEAM1011) yield higher-quality waveforms in dense canopy.
  • Urban interpretation: GEDI AGBD in urban areas reflects trees in parks, street trees, and green rooftops — not building biomass. Low AGBD pixels in NYC correspond to impervious surfaces where GEDI detected no canopy.
  • Version: Always use V002 — it includes updated allometric models and expanded geographic coverage.

References

  • Dubayah, R. et al. (2022). GEDI L4A Footprint Level Aboveground Biomass Density. ORNL DAAC. https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2056
  • GEDI Mission: https://gedi.umd.edu
  • NEON SCBI site: https://www.neonscience.org/field-sites/scbi
  • NASA EarthData: https://earthdata.nasa.gov
  • rGEDI R package: https://github.com/carlos-alberto-silva/rGEDI

item.title: Welcome to My Blog
item.description:
This is the first post on my blog. I will use this space to share thoughts on remote sensing, LiDAR analysis, forest ecology, and my research journey as a PhD student at Oklahoma State University.

Stay tuned for updates on ongoing projects, field work, and data science tips.
